technical_errors: Lines 54-55: the slot-table footnote claims `_shared/team-profile.md` supplies four facts to this skill — Simulator, Filelist convention, Register model source, Area to owner map — but only 'Register model source' is ever used again (step 5's Register model row, line 186). Lines 49 vs 151-154: the Config convention slot explicitly offers 'or both' as a legitimate answer for how a component gets its configuration ('from its parent's configuration object, from the configuration database keyed on its own instance path, or both'), but step 4 states as an absolute rule 'each component reads its configuration from exactly one place ... Never both' (line 151-153). A reader who fills the slot honestly as 'both' (a common real convention — structural knobs from the parent object, selection knobs from the config db) will read step 4 as calling their own house convention wrong. verb_honesty: Clean — every retrieval action is Read/Grep/Glob and every simulate/compile/query-a-licence-manager action is properly handed off to a human (line 146-147 licence entitlement, line 195-196 'ask the integration owner one question in writing', line 235-237 'ask the engineer to compile the empty environment skeleton once and give you the path to the build log'). hallucination_risks: None found at reportable confidence. The skill is unusually disciplined about not inventing house-specific facts: tool flags, VIP knob names, and message strings are absent; every fact that would require insider knowledge (VIP version, entitlement count, config key naming rule, reset ownership, delivery form, record location) is routed through a [[FILL:]] slot or an explicit human handoff. UVM terminology used directly (config db, virtual sequencer, build/connect/run phase, is_active) is industry-standard, not house-specific, so citing it directly (unlike a house tool flag) is legitimate and consistent with the golden references.
budget_violations: Lines 74-77 vs 100-102: the retrieval budget allocates step 1 exactly two Glob, two Grep, two Read calls total (one Grep for the module header, one conditional Grep for counting direction-keyword lines). But the step 1 body then instructs, for the very common case of SystemVerilog interface ports: 'Grep that same window for the interface type names instead, one interface each' (lines 100-102) — i.e. one Grep per distinct interface type on the top. Any top with more than one SV-interface type (the normal case for a block with more than a single external protocol) cannot execute this instruction inside the two-Grep allotment already spent on the module header, and even borrowing the pack's single floating reserve Grep (line 77) only extends the ceiling to three interface types before the rule breaks again. This is a concrete, mechanically-checkable violation of the CLAUDE.md requirement that 'the budget accounts for every Grep the steps actually spend' — the step's own prescribed action for a common case is not covered by its own stated allocation.

Lines 74 vs 93: the retrieval budget states all 8 windowed Reads are 'of about 80 lines' (line 74), but step 1's first Read is specified as 'about 100 lines' (line 93) — a 25% overshoot from the budget's own stated window size, inconsistent with the otherwise exact bookkeeping elsewhere in the document (the Glob/Grep/Read totals per step sum precisely to the stated 4/12/8 caps).

Lines 133-134 (secondary, lower confidence): 'Four facts belong in the record beside each VIP choice' implies repeating the version/entitlement/mechanism/visibility check per VIP-supplied interface, but step 3's budget is flat — one Glob, two Greps, one Read for the whole step (lines 74-76) — regardless of how many distinct VIPs are in play. A block using two different protocol VIPs (common at an IP company) would need to repeat the Glob-confirms-tree-on-disk and reference-environment-instantiation checks per VIP, which the flat per-step allocation does not obviously cover.
review.open_twice: "Likely yes, on balance. The architectural judgment is genuinely strong and matches the density/voice of the golden references — the topology/VIP/config/reuse-contract framework, the reuse-contract table, and the Gotchas section (monitor-cannot-go-passive, forked-VIP, entitlement-count-as-throughput-cap, reset-ownership-drift, bound-assertion fragility) are all technically sound and specific enough to be worth a second read. But a careful engineer who tries to follow the retrieval budget literally will hit the step 1 SV-interface contradiction on close to every real top-level module (most blocks expose more than one SV interface type), and will reach step 6 with no instruction for how to fill the 'reversal' field the record's own Human Verification section says is the record's 'clearest tell' of quality. Those two gaps are exactly the kind of thing that makes an engineer stop trusting a procedure mid-way through, even though the surrounding content is worth keeping."

The step explicitly forbids per-type calls and says why (a block with more than one external protocol is the normal case), and routes an over-long alternation to the new budget rule 4. recheck.why: Lint is clean (skills\dv-tb-architecture-record\SKILL.md [approve 1.000], 0 errors, 0 advisories), metadata role/level are exactly dv-engineer/principal, all 8 declared slots plus the one named profile row (Register model source) are spent, nothing is asserted that the author could not know, all seven routed siblings exist on disk, and the DV domain content is technically correct — I found nothing wrong in the UVM/VIP/config-phase claims, the passive-monitor gotcha, the objection-ownership rule or the RAL base-address row. Verb honesty is clean: every Run/compile/merge occurrence is a noun or the correct handoff phrasing. But three things still break. (a) The deliverable itself is incomplete: the fenced record block has no line for the approver or for its own proposal status, while step 6 requires both ("with the approver named inside it"; "this is a proposal until that person accepts it, and the record's first line says so") and "Done when" presupposes it ("The approver named in the record"). The block's first line is only "tb architecture record v1 — block, author, date". An engineer copy-pasting the block produces a record that structurally cannot say who must approve it or that it is unapproved — in a skill whose entire deliverable is a record for an approver. (b) Step 2 gives an interpretation rule it does not fund: "What is identical across the two reference environments is house convention; what differs is content. A convention seen in one file is a coincidence" — but it allocates "two Greps ... and two bounded Reads, at that environment's build phase and its connect phase", singular, against one environment. Grep takes one path; budget rule 4's name-alternation cannot merge two directory paths. Actually checking both costs 4 Greps and 4 Reads in step 2, taking the pack totals to 13 Greps and 9 Reads against declared caps of 12 and 8. Standing rule 3 — a step that cannot be carried out inside the skill's own caps is broken — is hit directly. (c) Step 5's table and step 5's prose point the same three Greps at two different environments, and step 6 then reasons from a third answer. The table says "Grep the reference environment for wildcard scopes and static members" and "Grep the reference environment for objection calls" unconditionally; the prose says "If one of them already exists in the tree, spend this step's Glob finding it, three Greps — wildcard scopes, static members, objection calls" against the higher-level target environment. Read literally that is 6 Greps in a 3-Grep step. Then step 6 asserts "Where step 5 found no higher-level environment it spent no Greps, so those costs have no file behind them and drop to the third tag below" — which is false whenever the reader followed the table, and instructs them to downgrade a genuine from-file reversal cost to judgement. Since the Human-verification section makes the reversal tag the headline check ("its clearest tell is a reversal column that is either absent or entirely untagged"), this defect lands on the output the skill is judged by.

new_problems: Step 2 (lines 136-140) demands a cross-check across TWO reference environments while funding 2 Greps + 2 Reads against one ("at that environment's build phase"). Step 6's "Where step 5 found no higher-level environment it spent no Greps" contradicts step 5's table, which greps the reference environment unconditionally. As written it tells the reader to tag a from-file count as judgement.
